overview: France is an attractive destination for students interested in **Study chemical engineering in France** due to its strong **chemical, pharmaceutical, energy, materials and environmental industries**.
Students can study programs in chemical engineering, process engineering, industrial chemistry and other scientific fields.
International students need to know the ** French higher education system ** : a three-year bachelor 's degree and a five-year engineering qualification are two different tracks.
Students may need to take basic scientific studies before entering a specialized engineering school for chemical engineering programs.
**Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance** can assist students in exploring these opportunities and understanding the requirements involved in pursuing education abroad.

sections.title: 1. Can I do chemical engineering in France after the 12th?

items: Yes, you can apply to eligible **bachelor’s programs, programs or preparatory pathways in science**. The decision to allow direct entry to a specific engineering school is based on the admission rules of that school.

sections.title: 2. How many years does it take to study chemical engineering in France?

items: A **bachelor's degree programme** usually takes three years. The French engineering qualification is generally a longer track, usually five years of higher education after secondary school.

sections.title: 3. Is French necessary to study chemistry engineering in France?

items: Many undergraduate programs are taught in French and may require proof of **French language proficiency**. Some programs or pathways have English taught components, so check the language requirements for each course.

sections.title: 4. How much do you pay for tuition fees for chemical engineering in France?

items: Fees vary depending on institution and qualification. **For 2026-2027** The published Licence reference for public universities is **€178 per year for eligible French and EU students** and **€2,902 for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees**. Engineering schools may charge different amounts, or be exempt.

sections.title: 5. What can I do with a chemical engineering degree after graduation?

items: As a graduate you can go into **process engineering, production, quality assurance, environmental management, industrial chemistry or research support** Some specialist engineering roles will require further study or an accepted engineering qualification.

Before registering, students are advised to check the status of the ****chemical engineering qualification in France**** they want to obtain it.
* Check that the *Diplôme d’ingénieur* is authorized and accredited by the **Commission des titres d’ingénieur (CTI)** for **French engineering education**.
* For bachelor level qualifications, verify if the program offers a recognized national degree or an officially recognized bachelor level grade.
See also:
* The exact title of the degree and awarding institution.
* **ECTS credits and duration of the programme**.
* Internship and Industrial training requirements.
* Possibility of studies in France or abroad.
*  Professional recognition requirements in the country you plan to work in.
**In France, chemical engineering graduates** are employed in **manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, energy, food processing, materials, environmental services and industrial research**.
**Possible job titles include:**
* Process or chemical engineer.
* Manufacturing/production engineer.
* Process development assistant or engineer**, based on your experience.
* Quality control or quality assurance professional.
* Expert in environment and sustainability.
* Research or laboratory technician.
* Materials or industrial chemistry specialist.
**engineering diploma or master’s level qualification** is required for some engineering positions and technical and laboratory jobs might have other entry qualifications.
****Salary expectations:**** Salary expectations vary depending on the qualification, experience, employer, location, industry and language skills.
Here are the **documents typically needed for undergraduate chemical engineering applications in France**:
* A valid passport.
* Secondary school certificate or equivalent qualification.
* Certificates and transcripts of class 10 and 12, if applicable.
* Proof of preparation in **math, chemistry and physics.**
* Results of language tests in French or English, if required.
* Curriculum Vitae if required.
* Letter of motivation or statement of purpose, if required.
* If needed, letters of recommendation.
* Certified translations of documents not accepted in original language.
* Application forms and any applicable application fee.
* Further financial, accommodation and visa documentation at the appropriate time.
Requirements vary by institution and by type of applicant. Only submit the documents required by the official admission portal.
